summary: Iteration 81 — backend-only verification of the new Vertex AI (Gemini 2.5 Flash, europe-west2) primary / OpenAI fallback routing in utils/ai.py. Created 2 pytest suites (31 tests, 30 pass / 1 fail = 96.8%). Verified: GCP env/service-account config valid and client builds; LIVE _gemini_chat() call to europe-west2 succeeds; _ai_chat() serves from Gemini with ZERO OpenAI calls (spy-instrumented) and no '[Vertex AI]' warning in logs; forced Vertex outage falls back transparently to OpenAI with the expected warning log; error only surfaces when BOTH providers fail. Full analyze_meeting() run on a realistic supervision transcript returned valid JSON with all required keys (summary/achievements/actions/learning_needs/risks/cqc_mappings/care_cert_mappings/custom_mappings), correct severity enums, confidence enums, safeguarding boundary-violation risk detected, learning need detected, and UK-language sanitiser applied (no 'pastoral'/'caseload'). Re-ran the same analysis with OpenAI hard-disabled — still succeeded, proving Gemini alone serves the main analysis. Secondary AI flows all verified live through the wrapper: PII scan (regex + AI, UK phone flagged), regenerate summary, prep-question coverage check (all 4 questions scored, unasked question correctly 'missed'), risk suggestions (excerpt + >=2 resolutions), document criteria extraction, and doc evidence scan (mappings produced). API-level end-to-end: admin (MFA bypass) POST /api/review/{id}/rescan-evidence completed in ~90s, GET /api/review/{id} returned a fully valid analysis payload, POST /api/review/{id}/regenerate-summary returned a real summary; regressions PDF export (signed-off meeting, %PDF bytes) and RBAC (attendee 403 on /api/admin/users) both pass. Backend logs contained ZERO '[Vertex AI]' lines across all runs => no fallback was ever triggered in live use.

minor.endpoint: utils/ai.py analyze_meeting / analyze_doc_for_evidence / scan_pii_in_transcript / analyze_custom_only / extract_document_criteria (lines 782, 811, 956, 1138, 1682)
minor.issue: Fragile JSON fence stripping: parsing only strips a code fence when the response text.startswith('```'). Reproduced with a stub response 'Here is the analysis:\n\n```json{...}```' -> json.JSONDecodeError -> analyze_meeting silently returns the degraded stub {summary: 'Analysis could not be parsed...', risks: [], all mappings: []}. Gemini is materially more likely than o4-mini to prepend a lead-in sentence before the JSON. This is a SILENT data-loss path: _ai_chat already succeeded so there is NO OpenAI retry, and the user sees an empty report rather than an error. 3 other call sites (lines 1855/1918/1959) already use the robust regex extractor r'```(?:json)?\s*([\s\S]*?)```' — unify all 5 fragile sites on that (plus a brace-slice fallback: text[text.find('{'):text.rfind('}')+1]).

_vertex_client_failed is a permanent process-level latch. A single transient failure at init time (e.g. metadata/network blip while parsing creds) permanently disables Vertex for the life of the worker process — every subsequent call silently uses OpenAI until the backend is restarted, with no repeated log line to reveal it. Add a retry/TTL or reset the latch periodically.

No success-path telemetry: nothing logs which provider actually served a response. The user's stated goal is to compare Gemini vs OpenAI outputs, and the only signal today is the ABSENCE of a warning line. Recommend logger.info('[AI] served by gemini-2.5-flash' / 'openai:<model>') and ideally persisting the provider name on the analysis row.

The reasoning_effort argument (used as 'high' for analyze_meeting, doc evidence, custom-only, prep questions and 'medium' for summary) is silently dropped on the Gemini path — no thinking_config/thinking_budget is set on GenerateContentConfig. Those call sites were deliberately routed to o4-mini with high reasoning; they now run on default-thinking gemini-2.5-flash. Functionally fine (verified), but it is an unmeasured output-quality change; consider types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_budget=...) to mirror the intent.

max_output_tokens=65536 is 1 above the documented gemini-2.5-flash cap (65535) and the budget is shared with thinking tokens. It did not error in testing, but on a long (80k-char) transcript the model can exhaust the budget on thinking and return empty text -> ValueError -> OpenAI fallback. Acceptable but worth an explicit thinking budget cap.

GCP_PROJECT_ID and GCP_LOCATION are written with surrounding double quotes. python-dotenv strips them so it works today, but any consumer reading the raw file (shell sourcing, k8s configmap generation) would get literal quotes. Recommend unquoting for consistency with the other keys.

action_items: HIGH: Replace the 5 fragile `text.startswith('```')` fence-strip blocks in utils/ai.py (lines 782, 811, 956, 1138, 1682) with the existing regex extractor + a brace-slice fallback. This is the single realistic way the Gemini switch can silently produce an empty analysis for a user.

MEDIUM: Add an info-level log (and ideally a persisted provider field) recording which provider served each AI call — required for the user's Gemini-vs-OpenAI comparison and for detecting silent permanent fallback.
MEDIUM: Make _vertex_client_failed recoverable (TTL/retry) instead of a permanent process latch.
LOW: Set an explicit ThinkingConfig on the Gemini path to mirror the previous reasoning_effort='high' intent, and lower max_output_tokens to <=65535.
LOW: Remove the quotes around GCP_PROJECT_ID / GCP_LOCATION in backend/.env.
critical_code_review_comments: _ai_chat() itself is correctly implemented for the stated requirement: it tries Gemini, catches `Exception` (broad, so safety blocks / quota / auth / asyncio.TimeoutError are all covered), logs a warning with the cause, and returns the OpenAI result. asyncio.CancelledError is a BaseException in 3.11 so genuine cancellation is not swallowed — good. Verified by test that a forced Vertex failure yields a correct OpenAI answer and the expected warning line.

All 12 previous _openai_chat(...) call sites in utils/ai.py are now _ai_chat(...); no direct _openai_chat call remains outside the fallback path, and no other module imports _openai_chat. Migration is complete.

The real end-to-end risk of this change is NOT the routing (which works) but the response-shape assumptions downstream: every JSON-embedded-in-text parser is tuned to OpenAI's habit of returning bare JSON. The parser hardening above should be treated as part of this feature, not a separate cleanup.

utils/ai.py is ~2000 lines and mixes provider clients, ~1200 lines of prompt constants, audio compression and 10+ business functions. Recommend splitting into ai/providers.py, ai/prompts.py and ai/analysis.py — it exceeds the 700-line guideline by ~3x and every AI change now touches one giant file.

rca_of_the_issue: test_prose_before_fence: analyze_meeting() only strips a markdown code fence when the response begins with '```' (utils/ai.py:1682). If the model emits any lead-in prose before the fence, json.loads() receives the prose and raises JSONDecodeError, and the except branch returns a hard-coded empty analysis ('Analysis could not be parsed...'). Because _ai_chat() already returned successfully, no OpenAI retry occurs. Gemini 2.5 Flash is more prone than o4-mini to adding a conversational preamble, so switching the primary provider raises the probability of this silent data loss. Fix: use the regex extractor already present at lines 1855/1918/1959, with a first-'{' to last-'}' slice as a final fallback, at all five fragile parse sites.
